L2t: Golf is played in many countries, with Scotland widely regarded as its historic birthplace and home to St Andrews.
L3t: Even in the countries most associated with golf, only a small minority of the population actually plays it regularly, so no country has a majority who love playing it.
L4t: There is no country where most people love playing golf; it remains a minority pastime everywhere.
L2f: Golf's modern rules were standardized in the 19th century and the sport has since spread to nearly every continent.
L3f: Scotland's national sports surveys show that a clear majority of Scots play golf regularly and enjoy it more than any other sport.
